verification_note: Phase 4 implements the Director_Movie Razor Page with full compliance to Engineering Quality Contract and phase Design Constraints. Key evidence: (1) All HTML id attributes match exact specifications: td_{camelCase}_{movieId} for movie cells (title, releaseDate, description, language, director, stars), btn_delete_{movieId} for delete buttons, di_{directorId} for director links — verified against phase spec and manual end-to-end test confirmation. (2) Release date formatted correctly as MM/dd/yyyy (verified at line 38 of Director_Movie.cshtml). (3) Stars joined with comma only, no spaces (line 42: string.Join(",", movie.Stars.Select(s => s.FullName))). (4) All HTTP operations routed through GivenApiClient injected via DI, no direct calls from view. (5) CancellationToken propagation maintained from Phase 3 fixes: all async methods in GivenApiClient accept and forward token parameter, used in GetAsync() and DeleteAsync() calls. (6) IDisposable cleanup enforced via 'using' statements for HttpResponseMessage in GetJsonAsync<T> (line 41) and DeleteMovieAsync (line 34). (7) Generic GetJsonAsync<T> helper (lines 39-45) extracted common deserialization logic without introducing abstraction overhead or coupling issues. (8) Refactored MovieResponse model correctly reuses DirectorResponse instead of duplicating DirectorInfo nested class — DRY adherence and reduces surface area. (9) Known, scoped exception (GET handler for delete via ?handler=Delete&id=) properly documented in Design Constraints and correctly implemented via OnGetDeleteAsync; aligns with exam requirement for <a> tag and no-JavaScript design. (10) 60/60 unit tests pass (Q2_MovieApp.Tests 22 tests plus Q1_WebAPI.Tests 38 tests), confirming implementation correctness. (11) Manual end-to-end verification against live givenAPI (port 5100): first-load table rendering with all required HTML ids, director filter correctly narrows scope (e.g., di_2 shows only Aaron Horvath's movies), live delete of movie id=9 confirmed removed from API store.
